sections.html:
Chesterfield County lies just south of Richmond, with the James River forming much of its northern border and the Appomattox River much of its southern one. The county seat is Chesterfield Court House, and the county has no incorporated towns.

It is large. The 2020 census counted 364,548 residents, the fourth most populous county in Virginia, and the county's 2025 estimate is 397,148. The county covers 437 square miles, of which 423 are land.

It crosses the Fall Line, with hillier Piedmont terrain to the west and flatter Tidewater coastal plain to the east. Neighbors include Henrico, Colonial Heights, Petersburg, Hopewell, Powhatan and Dinwiddie.

sections.h2: What is the history of Chesterfield County?
sections.html:
Chesterfield was created from part of Henrico County on May 25, 1749, and named for Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield. It has an unusually long record of firsts: coal mining began in the 1730s, the Manchester Turnpike opened in 1807 as Virginia's first graveled road of significant length, and the Chesterfield Railroad opened in 1831 as Virginia's first railroad.

Richmond annexed 23 square miles of the county in 1970 under the Horner-Bagley Compromise, and in 1981 Chesterfield gained immunity from further annexation by Richmond. After World War II the county grew quickly as a commuter suburb. That history explains why many Chesterfield houses are postwar and later subdivisions, with a few older farm properties scattered between them.

sections.h2: Which communities, roads and employers define Chesterfield County?
sections.html:
The best known communities are Chester, the largest, followed by Midlothian, Bon Air, Brandermill, Ettrick, Bermuda Hundred and Matoaca. The northern portion is often called North Chesterfield.

  • Interstate 95 runs through the county, and Interstate 85 begins near Petersburg.
  • U.S. 60 (Midlothian Turnpike) follows the route of the 1807 turnpike.
  • The Powhite Parkway extension (State Route 76) and the Pocahontas Parkway (State Route 895), an 8.8 mile toll road, cross the area.
  • GRTC Route 111 has linked the Chippenham Parkway area to Brightpoint Community College in Chester since March 2020.

Employers with 1,000 or more workers include Amazon Fulfillment Services, HCA Virginia Health System, UPS, Walmart, DuPont Specialty Products, Kroger, Bon Secours Richmond Health System, Food Lion and Capital One. Commonwealth Fusion Systems plans a grid-scale fusion power plant at the James River Industrial Center, and the county approved its conditional use permit in 2025.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Chesterfield County usually deal with?
sections.html:
The county's growth since World War II, when it became a commuter suburb of Richmond, means a large share of its houses are decades old. Original roofs, aging heating and cooling equipment and dated kitchens are common reasons a house sits unsold, and a buyer using a mortgage may ask for repairs that an as is cash buyer does not.

Chesterfield's size also matters. With more than 364,000 residents, an owner who inherits a house, or who has moved away, may be managing a property from far off while tax statements keep arriving. Getting the Treasurer's current balance early is a useful first step, and the county's payment plan page is worth reading before the next due date.

sections.h2: How does the Chesterfield assessment cycle work?
sections.html:
Chesterfield reassesses real estate every year. Assessment notices are mailed by February 1 and show values as of January 1, and the county says assessments must reflect 100 percent of fair market value.

The Board of Supervisors sets the tax rate, and the county lists $0.89 per $100 of assessed value for 2026. Values are based on inspections, sales data and comparisons with similar nearby properties. Commercial owners are asked to complete an income and expense survey online by July 15.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Chesterfield County assessment?
sections.html:
File with Real Estate Assessments by March 15, then go to the Board of Equalization by April 15 if you disagree. The county says late applications are not processed, and that the first level is required before you can appeal further.

  1. Review your values on the county's READ site or contact the office.
  2. Get the application and file a separate one for each property.
  3. Attach support: up to three comparable properties, a recent appraisal or photos, and for income property three years of income and expense statements plus a current rent roll.
  4. If a representative files for you, add a notarized Letter of Authorization.
  5. An appraiser may ask questions or inspect, then notifies you of the outcome.

The Board of Equalization is an independent board under the Code of Virginia. Its members are appointed by a Circuit Court judge and trained by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Under 58.1-3379, the assessor's value is presumed correct and the owner must rebut it. Real Estate Assessments is at 6801 Mimms Loop, with phone 804-748-1321 and email assessor@chesterfield.gov.

sections.h2: What else shapes a Chesterfield County bill?
sections.html:
Geography decides which services and which mailing address apply, and it helps to know a few quirks before a sale. Ettrick, for example, is mostly served by a Petersburg mailing address even though it lies in Chesterfield County, so a seller there should check which locality actually bills the parcel. The county tax office, not the postal city, is the one to ask.

The Real Estate Assessments page also names a contact for the Lower Magnolia Green Community Development Authority, so ask the closing agent whether your parcel sits in a special district or carries a charge beyond the normal county bill.

  • Automated Payment Service: free, with taxes debited on the due date after about 30 to 45 days of activation.
  • APS returns: a $50 return-item fee applies for insufficient funds, in addition to any bank fees.
  • Citizen Portal: shows invoices for the most recent six years.
  • Payment kiosks: take cash, cards and checks, around the clock.

These details matter when an heir is cleaning up an old account. The six year view lets you see what was billed, and the Treasurer can explain anything older.

sections.h2: When are Chesterfield County real estate taxes due and how do you pay?
sections.html:
The county's homepage lists the current real estate tax as due Monday, December 7, 2026, and warns of a 10 percent penalty if it is missed.

The Treasurer's Office is at 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832, with mail to P.O. Box 70. The phone is 804-748-1201, and hours are weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • Online through the Citizen Portal, which now requires an account.
  • By phone at 855-933-5661, around the clock.
  • Through your bank's bill pay, mailed to P.O. Box 70.
  • At payment kiosks in seven county library and administration locations.
  • By drop box at the Lane B. Ramsey Administration Building, checks or money orders only.

Processor fees are 2 percent for credit cards and a flat $2.50 for debit cards, while eCheck has no fee. Virginia's 58.1-3916 caps interest at 10 percent a year and the property penalty at 10 percent.

sections.h2: What can a Chesterfield seller do if the tax bill is behind?
sections.html:
A seller who cannot pay on time can apply for a tax payment plan through the county, though interest and fees keep accruing during the plan. The county says staff respond within two business days and that approval is not guaranteed.

A plan also does not release a DMV stop, which is lifted only when accounts are paid in full. That is worth knowing if you have both vehicle and real estate balances.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 under 58.1-802. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure that matches your closing date, since interest grows daily. Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesterfield County house as is, including one with back tax or repairs, and settle the payoff from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Chesterfield County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county lists $0.89 per $100 of assessed value for 2026, set by the Board of Supervisors.

faqs.q: When do I have to appeal a Chesterfield assessment?
faqs.a: March 15 for Real Estate Assessments, and April 15 for the Board of Equalization. The county does not process late applications.

faqs.q: Where is the Chesterfield County Treasurer?
faqs.a: At 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832. The phone is 804-748-1201 and the office is open weekdays, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Does a Chesterfield payment plan stop penalties?
faqs.a: No. The county says interest and fees keep accruing during a plan, and a plan does not release a DMV stop.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Chesterfield County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, the balance is normally paid from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before the closing date.
